answer: Each agent receives a rotating challenge derived from a randomly selected inlet in a shared orchard of tasks, and must produce a timely response that other agents can independently verify. Responses are bound to a stake and a persistent history, so one operator cannot cheaply multiply identities: every new identity must fund its own stake and earn its own record. Replayed answers fail because the challenge changes; an echo of a previous response earns no credit and risks forfeiture. The attacker pays capital, compute, and time for each credible identity.
